AA · T07 · segment holding · pre-registration sha256 1d302f1055c3 · data: APPROVED_DATA.md as of 2026-11-12

Does holding each stock only while its own market-cap index is BUY choose what to hold better than a random exclusion of the same weight?

2019-01-02 → 2026-10-30 (SCMO_0007 from 2019-01-04) · four parents of the AA books · decisions every Friday, trades next session at OHLC4 · 10.4 bps a side · 2,000 draws per book, cost and null · every number is computed from evidence/headline/ · run on 2026-11-12 data

The answer

No: Study 3's rejection stands on a matched null. Holding each stock a parent holds only while the index of its size band is BUY (Large: Nifty 100, Mid: Midcap 100, Small and below: Smallcap 100), and sending the weight of the rest to a 50/50 GOLDBEES and cash sleeve, against dropping a random set of the same weight at the same events (N4.6, decides), on 2019-01-02 → 2026-10-30, after 20.8 bps. C1 (return beats the 90th percentile of the null): 2 of 4 books; C2 (worst fall): 1 of 4; C3 (rule minus the whole-book switch above zero): 0 of 4 (pre-registered pass: 3 of 4 each). N4.8 (label permutation, beside it): C1 2 of 4, C2 1 of 4.

The catch: the three signals disagree in only 88 of 410 weeks, in 16 stretches shared by all four books, so the rule differs from the whole-book switch in only 16 independent places and "3 of 4" is a consistency check. On the live decisions only (2021-11-01 → 2026-10-30) C1 reaches the 90th percentile in 1 of 4 books and C3 is positive in 0 of 4. Nothing is out of sample (Study 3 saw 2021-11 → 2026-08); the decisions before 2021-11 are a backfill; about 93% to 93% of the exposure is tagged by the market-cap rank rule, which agrees with real index membership on 92.07% of member-snapshots in 2026 only; so every result is PROVISIONAL.

What to be careful about

  • The null is "drop a random set of the same weight at the same events". A pass on C1 says the tag chooses better than a random set of the same size, not that it beats holding the whole book or the parent; C3 and the constant mix below answer that.
  • Nothing is out of sample. Study 3 ran this idea on 2021-11 → 2026-08. The decisions before 2021-11 are a backfill by the production code. On the live window the rule passes C1 in 1 of 4 books against N4.6.
  • 16 disagreement stretches is all the evidence there is. The smallest return edge detectable at 80% power against N4.6 is 1.2 to 2.6 pp a year, but N4.6 draws from only 1 to 6,435 allowed subsets per event, so its spread is narrow.
  • The tags. the rank rule is untested before 2026-04-09: its 92.07% three-band agreement with real membership (Large recall 88.1%, Mid 79.8%, Small and below 96.5%) is measured on eight 2026 snapshots; on the parents' own holdings it is 88.9% by weight (SCMO_0003 91.1%, 0007 88.2%, 0010 80.0%, 0029 96.3%);

The data

Each parent's NAV is rebuilt every day from its own stocks (Eikon prices, price return, Polyplex's special dividend corrected), not read from a file. The published NAV (D17) gives the calendar and a check: the engine's always-invested book reproduces it within the pre-registered tolerance. Every file below is an APPROVED row of data/APPROVED_DATA.md, whose "As of" date is 2026-11-12 (the run recorded 2026-11-12). No price after 2026-10-30 is read.

Caveats of the tag data (T07.md section 3, from the independent review data/review/2026-11-12_tag_sources/REVIEW.md):

  1. the market-cap history to 2025-11-28 was back-filled (written 2026-01-02/03 and 2025-12-31), so a point-in-time vintage cannot be proven;
  2. the rank rule is untested before 2026-04-09: its 92.07% three-band agreement with real membership (Large recall 88.1%, Mid 79.8%, Small and below 96.5%) is measured on eight 2026 snapshots; on the parents' own holdings it is 88.9% by weight (SCMO_0003 91.1%, 0007 88.2%, 0010 80.0%, 0029 96.3%);
  3. the tag source switches on 2026-04-09 and about 8% of stocks differ between the two sources;
  4. isolated bad market-cap rows exist (LODHA 2021, AXISBANK 2026-10-07), none changes a parent holding's band;
  5. JSWSTEEL, VEDL and ZEEL (listed in D21 under preference-share ISINs) and EMBASSY, BIRET and BAGMANE (not in D20) are not in any basket to 2026-10-30 and would read by rank in a later basket.

Controls. V6, the negative control: 100 circular shifts of the joint three-signal weekly matrix (information-free signals that look like the real ones), each run through the rule and judged against its own N4.6 null; a book passes if at most 17 of the 100 reach the 90th percentile of CAGR (17 is the largest count that chance, at 10% a shift, produces with probability at least 0.05 ÷ 4: a one-sided exact binomial test across the four books). This rule was amended on 2026-11-12, before any result was read, and after a trial run had shown one book at 17 of 100: the pre-registered band was [4%, 16%] for each book, two-sided, which fails one of four fair books about one time in five by chance. The amendment is in T07.md, "Amendments before the run".

One rule, end to end (SCMO_0003, 20.8 bps, 2019-01-02 → 2026-10-30)

1. The decision and the event. The latest weekly decision before the event is week 10, Friday 2019-03-08: the latest Master rows read Nifty 100 SELL (row 2019-03-08), Midcap 100 BUY (2019-03-08), Smallcap 100 BUY (2019-03-08). Event 2 of 57 (kind: signal) is traded on session 2019-03-11 (index 47); its information date is the session before, 2019-03-08; the basket in force became available on 2018-12-17. Its states: Nifty 100 SELL, Midcap 100 BUY, Smallcap 100 BUY.

band on ⇔ SIGN of its index (latest Master row dated on or before the decision date) = BUY Large → Nifty 100, Mid → Midcap 100, Small and below → Smallcap 100 kept stock → V × listed weight dropped stock → its weight goes half to GOLDBEES, half to cash

3. The targets. The listed weights of a basket are renormalised to a row sum of 1 (as T06 does; the engine's reading E5 in audit.json), so Σw = 1. Sum of listed weights Σw = 1.000000; weight dropped D = 0.097778 (1 of 10 stocks); s = D ÷ Σw = 0.097778. Kept stock i gets V × w_i; GOLDBEES and cash units each get V × s ÷ 2 = V × 0.048889; every new position is then scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V.

s = D ÷ Σw GOLDBEES target = cash target = V × s ÷ 2 stock i (kept) target = V × w_i

4. The trade. On 2019-03-11 at each instrument's (open + high + low + close) ÷ 4: value before cost V = 1.007796; value traded (both sides) 1.818511; cost = traded × 20.8 ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 = 0.001891 (engine: 0.001891).

6. Statistics. The path runs from 1.000000 on 2019-01-02 to 5.842947 on 2026-10-30: 1932 sessions, years = (1932 − 1) ÷ 252 = 7.6627, CAGR = 5.8429^(1 ÷ 7.6627) − 1 = 25.91%, worst fall -19.94%.

7. One N4.6 draw. The null keeps this event, the stocks held and the weight the rule drops, and drops a random subset of about that weight instead: every subset whose listed weight is within τ = half the smallest listed weight = 0.048889 of D. The stocks are indexed in ISIN order, subsets are listed by increasing bitmask (bit i = stock i), and the draw takes element floor(u × count) of the list, with u the next rng.random() of default_rng([7, draw_id, book_no]), one per event.

Here 10 of 2^10 = 1024 subsets are allowed. Draw 0 uses uniform number 2 of 57: u = 0.897214; index floor(0.897214 × 10) = 8; bitmask 256. It drops PARAGMILK.NS (listed weight 0.097778), where the rule drops JSWSTEEL.NS (weight 0.097778); the gap 0.000000 is within τ. The drops stored for draw 0 equal this replay: yes.

Over the whole window draw 0 earns 24.78% a year with a worst fall of -19.09% and 56 trades (the rule: 56 trades); N4.8 draw 0 earns 24.91%, worst fall -18.42%.

8. The ranking. Against N4.6 the rule's CAGR beat 1,484 of 2,000 draws, tied 0, and was beaten by 516: percentile = (1484 + 0.5 × 0) ÷ 2,000 × 100 = 74.20; p-value = (1 + 516 + 0) ÷ (2,000 + 1) = 0.2584. Against N4.8: beat 1,434, tied 0, beaten by 566: percentile 71.70, p = 0.2834.

9. The comparators. The whole-book switch holds every stock while all three signals are BUY and the 50/50 sleeve otherwise (T06's strategy); the parent holds every stock throughout; the constant mix holds the rule's average share all the time. A stretch is a run of consecutive weekly decisions whose three signals are neither all BUY nor all SELL; its sessions run from the first decision's trade session to the next decision's. The stretches are the same in the four books (SCMO_0007 starts two days later); the independent unit of this test is the stretch, not the book.

Why the whole-book switch beats the segment rule, and when

Post hoc and descriptive: it is not part of the pre-registered test and changes no verdict. Window 2019-01-02 → 2026-10-30, 20.8 bps, the same runs as everything above. The whole-book switch holds the parent only while Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 are all BUY, and sits in the 50/50 gold and cash sleeve otherwise. The segment rule keeps each stock whose own index is BUY.

The two rules hold the same weights whenever the three signals agree (all BUY: both fully invested; all SELL: both in the sleeve). So the gap between them can only open in the 16 disagreement stretches, and it does: the stretches carry all of it, and what happens outside them is -0.4 to +0.5 log points in the four books against a total of -22 to -11. Every figure in this section is in log points: 100 x ln(rule value / whole-book switch value). Positive = the rule is ahead (blue), negative = the whole-book switch is ahead (red).

Entries are 100 x ln(rule value / whole-book value) summed over the stretches of each kind; they add up exactly across stretches. Positive = the rule gained on the whole-book switch, negative = the whole-book switch gained on the rule. A stretch's kind is read from the signals just before it and just after it.

The reading

  • The whole-book switch wins mainly on false starts. In 5 stretches (2, 7, 8, 12, 15) one or two indices turned BUY, the third never joined, and the market fell back to all SELL. The rule had bought the stocks of the BUY indices; the whole-book switch waited in the sleeve. That costs the rule 37 to 43 log points in the four books (shown as -43 to -37 above), more than its total deficit of 11 to 22.
  • The rule wins on shake-outs, but only twice. In stretches 5, 10 all three signals were BUY, one index turned SELL, the whole-book switch left, the other two stayed BUY and the market kept rising. The rule's gain is +24 to +41 log points. Without those two stretches the rule's total would be -52 to -40 instead of -22 to -11 (table below).
  • What the rule loses in a false start is the gap between the stocks it buys and the sleeve it gives up. Across the 5 false starts the kept stocks earned, on average over the four books, -8.6 (Large), -12.7 (Mid) and -18.2 (Small and below) percentage points of the book against the sleeve. The longest false start, stretch 15 (2025-09-22 → 2026-01-27, 18 weeks), is the one where the sleeve itself returned +21% (half of it GOLDBEES) while the rule's kept stocks lagged it.
  • This is 16 stretches, not 64 observations. The four books share the signals and differ only in which stocks they hold, so a stretch is one piece of evidence; "40 of 64" counts it four times.

Total less the named stretches. The deficit is the small sum of two large opposite sets, the false starts (-43 to -37) and the shake-outs (+24 to +41). Without the false starts the rule is ahead in every book (+21 to +32); without the shake-outs the whole-book switch is far ahead (-52 to -40). Without stretch 15 alone the rule is ahead in SCMO_0029. The sign of the result therefore rests on a handful of stretches.

"Kept stocks against the sleeve" = for every stock the rule holds, its daily return minus the rule's own sleeve return, times its value the day before, summed over the stretch and divided by the rule's value at its start (percentage points of the book). This is a different quantity from the log points above: it is in percentage points of the book, and "Other (pp)" in the per-book tables is the rule's return minus the whole-book switch's return minus the kept-stocks figure (trading costs, fills against closes, the whole-book switch's own sleeve). The positions reproduce the rule's value to 4e-16 (relative), so the attribution rests on the exact holdings; before the first logged trade (2019-03-11) the book holds only the sleeve.

Definitions

  • Event: a trade session on which targets are rebuilt: T0; a session after a weekly decision on which the set of stocks the current tags would drop differs from the set currently dropped; the first session on or after a basket's availableDate. Tags are read at events only, as of the session before.
  • Tag: Large, Mid or Small and below. From 2026-04-09 the band of the index the stock is listed in on the latest membership snapshot (Nifty 100 Large, Midcap 150 Mid, Smallcap 250 and Microcap 250 Small and below); before, the band of its market-cap rank on the latest snapshot on or before the date (1 to 100, 101 to 250, above 250); a stock in none of the indices uses the rank.
  • Percentile: (draws worse + 0.5 × draws tied) ÷ draws × 100, ties equal within a relative 1e-12. p-value: (1 + draws at least as good) ÷ (draws + 1).
  • CAGR: NAV_end^(252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1, daily NAV, after cost. Worst fall (maximum drawdown): the most negative NAV ÷ running peak − 1. Volatility: SD of daily returns × √252. Ulcer index: root mean square of the percentage drawdown. Calmar: CAGR ÷ |maximum drawdown|.
  • N4.6 size-matched random exclusion (decides): at every event a random subset of the held stocks whose total listed weight is within τ = half the smallest listed weight of the weight the rule drops, uniform over all such subsets, redrawn at every event. Seed default_rng([7, draw_id, book_no]).
  • N4.8 persistent label permutation (beside it): one random score per ISIN per draw; at every event the held stocks are ranked by score and given the labels Large, Mid, Small and below in the rule's counts per band; the real signals act on the labels. Seed default_rng([8, draw_id, book_no]).
  • Whole-book switch: every stock follows the single state IN iff all three signals are BUY, else 50/50 GOLDBEES and cash (T06's strategy). C3: the rule's after-cost CAGR minus the whole-book switch's. MDE: 2.8 × the SD of the draws' CAGR (or maximum drawdown). Live window: 2021-11-01 → 2026-10-30.
